messages:
Alex: Heads-up — SBOM scan flagged a high severity CVE in a native crypto binding we vendor via wheelhouse: CVE-2025-12345. It looks like a transitive dependency of libcrypto-bindings v0.9.2.
Maya: do we actually use the vulnerable code path at runtime?
Alex: quick triage: we only ship the wheel for compatibility with older worker images. Our runtime uses OpenSSL through the OS package, not the python binding.
Jamal: can you paste the SBOM snippet?
Alex: sure: ```
package: libcrypto-bindings@0.9.2
source: pypi
licenses: MIT
vulns: - CVE-2025-12345 (High) - patch available 0.9.3
used_by: - wheelhouse-build
```
Sophie: thanks. Sounds like a false positive for runtime usage, but still risky if someone rebuilds a worker with that wheel in the future.
Maya: what's the exploitability? is it RCE in pure-python or needs native call?
Jamal: notes from vendor: exploit requires calling `bind_key_unwrap()` with an attacker-controlled state — not exposed via our public SDK. needs native access.
Alex: so chain is low for us, but P0 scanners flag as high. Sec wants short-lived mitigations so we don't fail audits.
Maya: proposed mitigations: (1) temporary allowlist in SBOM scanner with justification, (2) add a strict build-time check to block wheel inclusion in new builds, (3) add a quick runtime detection for the wheel at startup to log and alert.
Sophie: agree. Also rotate KMS keys for any worker images built in the last 30 days as a compensating control? seems heavy.
Jamal: I can do a narrow compensating control: prevent wheel from being used in Dedicated/private images by adding an image whitelist in our builder. That avoids key rotation.
Alex: sec-bot: create an exception ticket and set expiration 2025-08-01.
sec-bot: Exception created: SEC-EX-2025-0743. Expires: 2025-08-01. Reviewer: @Maya.
Maya: I'll review. For the allowlist request we need: (a) justification, (b) compensating controls, (c) expiration, (d) migration plan. Alex can you draft?
Alex: drafting now: justification = false positive due to runtime not using native API; controls = build-time block for new wheels, image whitelist for private/dedicated, runtime detector alerting to PagerDuty, no external-facing endpoints use the library; expiration = 30 days. migration plan = vendor upgrade to 0.9.3 or remove wheel from wheelhouse and pin to system OpenSSL.
Jamal: add: CI will fail if wheel is present in wheelhouse after 2025-07-15. I'll raise a PR to the builder pipeline.
Sophie: for audit logs — add an audit entry for any worker image build that includes the wheel. That way we can review the last 90 days of builds.
Alex: I added a small startup check in the staging worker image to log the package presence and sha256. snippet: ```python
import pkgutil, hashlib, importlib
if pkgutil.find_loader('libcrypto_bindings'):
    import libcrypto_bindings as lcb
    print('libcrypto_bindings present', hashlib.sha256(lcb.__file__.encode()).hexdigest())
```
Maya: OK. Next steps: Alex -> finalize exception writeup and attach SBOM evidence. Jamal -> PR to builder to block inclusion + CI gate. Sophie -> enable build-time audit log and runtime detector in staging. I'll review and sign off if everything's in place.
Alex: will post the exception doc here when done.
Dependabot: bump libcrypto-bindings to 0.9.3 in wheelhouse (automated PR created) — https://github.com/redwood-inference/wheelhouse/pull/1423 :thumbsup:
Jamal: great, if vendor patch merges and CI verifies, we can close the exception early.
Sophie: thanks team. Small note: add a KMS note — any images built with the wheel should not be eligible for automatic KMS key rotation until we confirm builds are clean. I'll coordinate with infra.
Alex: noted. closing checklist: exception ticket, builder PR, staging runtime detector, audit logs enabled, vendor bump verification.
Maya: thanks — set reminder 2025-07-31 to re-evaluate. :calendar:
